channel.description: 每6小时更新，推荐 alphaxiv 上最近30天 cs.IR 热门论文

item.title: OneQuery: Unified Sequence-to-Structure Generation for Multilingual E-commerce Query Understanding
item.description: Multilingual e-commerce search requires robust query understanding to convert cross-lingual user queries with varied linguistic patterns into standardized semantic representations that support retrieval and ranking. However, traditional Query Understanding systems suffer from error accumulation, separately optimized subtasks that ignore their mutual correlations, and high maintenance costs. To address these issues, this paper proposes OneQuery, a unified generative framework for multilingual que...

item.title: Community Notes Across Platforms: Evaluating the Feasibility of Re-using Crowd-sourced Context Notes
item.description: Crowdsourced fact-checking systems such as Community Notes can provide useful context for misleading content. Producing and rating new notes on such systems requires substantial contributor effort. However, the resulting context is typically confined to the post and platform for which it was created. We ask whether already-vetted notes can be reused when the same claims recur across posts and platforms. To investigate this question, we construct a human-labelled dataset using Community Notes att...

item.title: ConTra: A Training Framework for Effective Contextual Retrieval via Prefix Generation
item.description: Data management systems organize large text collections for tasks such as finding relevant studies and extracting contract clauses. Systems make long documents searchable by splitting them into independently indexed chunks. Chunking can separate text from its identifying details. The indexing challenge is to keep each chunk independently searchable while preserving the context needed to find and rank it. Existing methods either encode that context in chunk vectors or attach it as a text prefix. ...

item.title: RecField: Embedding Recommendations into Spatial Movie Organization as Affordances for Serendipitous Encounters
item.description: Research on serendipity-oriented recommender systems has focused on algorithms that recommend unexpected yet useful items. However, serendipity is increasingly viewed as a user experience shaped by both algorithmic outputs and system features. This study positions recommendations not as the primary goal users pursue but as an environmental affordance that creates opportunities for discovery during other activities. We propose RecField, a spatial movie organization interface where users freely ar...

item.title: Welfare-Enhancing Mechanism Design for Agent Ecosystems
item.description: The emerging Agentic Web forms a multi-agent ecosystem: a decentralized service market where the user agent selects which content agents to query from their submitted profiles, before seeing any documents. Profiles therefore become a new target of optimization. Existing Generative Engine Optimization studies how a single supplier rewrites documents the engine can already retrieve, to improve their citation. In the Agentic Web, multiple content agents optimize profiles to compete for limited oppo...

item.title: Procedure Inference as Memory: Learning Recruiter Decision Procedures from OKF-Structured Episodes in Multi-Session Hiring Assistants
item.description: Multi-session hiring assistants must infer evolving recruiter preferences and decision patterns across projects and time. We introduce Open Knowledge Format (OKF)-indexed episodic memory to organize interactions and retrieve related events through their lineage. We also introduce Procedure Memory, which learns reusable decision procedures from these episodes through prompted reflection or reinforcement learning. We compare these approaches with no memory, full-history context, and conversation s...

item.title: Grounding User Preferences in Shared Multimodal Concepts for Recommendation
item.description: Multimodal recommendation has substantially advanced item understanding by incorporating rich visual and textual content. Yet user preferences are still commonly encoded as implicit signals tied to individual items, leaving recurring semantic factors without persistent identities that can be shared across items. We introduce MKGE, a multimodal knowledge graph framework that represents these factors as canonical, addressable concepts. MKGE induces a domain-adaptive concept vocabulary from item im...

item.title: Agentic Waterfall: An Intent-Driven Information Discovery Framework for Reclaiming User Control in the Attention Economy
item.description: We formalize Agentic Waterfall Feed, a new problem of personalized information discovery in which users actively direct recommendations and the system adapts to evolving needs inferred from both explicit requests and browsing behavior. We address this problem with the Agentic Waterfall framework, whose language-model controller maintains persistent user state and coordinates content retrieval, ranking, and state updates. To evaluate systems on this task, we contribute the Agentic Waterfall Datas...

item.title: MulCLIP: A Multi-level Alignment Framework for Enhancing Fine-grained Long-context CLIP
item.description: Vision-language models such as CLIP excel at image-text alignment but struggle with long, detailed descriptions due to training on short captions. Recent methods address this limitation using region proposals to align visual regions with sentences, but at substantial deployment cost. We present MulCLIP, an end-to-end multi-level alignment framework that directly exploits natural long-text structure without region proposals. Instead of simply stacking objectives, MulCLIP aligns different textual ...

item.title: Privacy-Aware Adaptive Client Selection for Federated Retrieval-Augmented Generation
item.description: Federated retrieval-augmented generation retrieves evidence from distributed corpora. However, broadcasting queries to all clients increases the retrieval burden and query exposure. We present Privacy-Aware Adaptive Client Selection for Federated Retrieval-Augmented Generation (PACS-FedRAG), an online selector that takes into account perturbed semantic profiles along with evidence feedback, latency, payload cost, and exploration. In a ten-client setting where three clients are chosen, the archiv...

item.title: Structure-Aware Multimodal Retrieval Under Data Scarcity, Privacy Constraints and Out-of-Domain Content
item.description: Purpose: Figure retrieval from reference atlases in expert domains like forensic pathology, dentistry and geology must work without labels or training pairs, on content that often cannot leave local hardware, and on images outside the training data of image-text encoders. This work proposes a structure-aware pipeline that satisfies all three, retrieving figures through the page structure recovered by layout geometry and a local open-weight 8B VLM. Methods: A geometry-based pairing method is intr...

item.title: Multi-Modal Causal Disentanglement for Multi-Domain Sequential Audio Recommendation
item.description: Modern music platforms expose users to heterogeneous audio content domains such as songs, playlists, and podcasts. Multi-domain sequential recommendation (MDSR) seeks to exploit such cross-domain behavior, yet two obstacles persist in practice. First, joint optimization across heterogeneous domains is prone to negative transfer, with high-traffic domains dominating the shared parameter space and suppressing weaker domains. Second, conventional ID-based collaborative signals fail to bridge domain...

item.title: CA-RAG: Constraint-Aligned Retrieval for Structurally Faithful Long-Form Generation
item.description: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) typically optimises evidence selection for semantic relevance, whereas compliance-sensitive long-form generation also requires evidence supporting explicit structural obligations. Semantically relevant retrieval may therefore omit information needed for mandatory downstream clauses. We propose Constraint-Aligned RAG (CA-RAG), a retrieval-conditioning framework that augments section-specific queries with ontology-derived structural constraints and policy-groun...

item.title: Learning the Platform, Not the Learner: Sequencing Shortcuts in the Offline Evaluation of Educational Recommender Systems and LLM Rankers
item.description: Educational recommenders are usually compared offline, by how well they predict the next activity in logs of tutoring systems, learning applications and MOOCs, where the next activity is largely decided by the platform: teachers assign problem sets, tutors draw problems until mastery, engines select questions. On eight public datasets from five platforms, we compare four structural predictors, which use nothing about the learner beyond the last activity, with ten personalised recommenders and wi...

item.title: Delegent: A Multi-Agent Harness That Reduces Cost without Sacrificing Performance
item.description: Agents built on frontier language models are expensive. At every step, the frontier model re-reads its entire context and executes every subtask regardless of its difficulty. This paper explores the simple thesis that much of this cost can be removed by delegating easy subtasks to a small language model, or SLM, that runs on hardware one already owns. To test it, we build Delegent, a simple and effective agent harness built on Claude Code, in which the frontier model stays in charge of every tas...

item.title: SAG-Mem-1.0 Technical Report
item.description: Long-term conversational memory requires retrieving complementary facts scattered across dialogue sessions, including intermediate evidence with limited similarity to the original question. Existing approaches often rely on derived memory representations or persistent relational structures, introducing construction costs and potentially losing source details. We present SAG-Mem, a conversational memory framework that preserves complete dialogue messages in non-overlapping chunks and discovers co...

item.title: SOARS: System One Assisted Reranking for Agentic Search
item.description: Deep search agents address complex information needs through iterative retrieval and reasoning, where the relevance of retrieved evidence influences downstream performance. Existing rerankers improve retrieval effectiveness but introduce substantial latency and cost when invoked throughout the search trajectory. We introduce SOARS, a training-free framework leveraging a System One model for fast, calibrated relevance estimation. At each search step, SOARS selects query-relevant passages from lon...

item.title: Towards Realistic Evaluation of Uncertainty Quantification for LLM-Based Recommender Systems
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) provide a flexible interface for recommendation systems. However, their issued rankings require reliable instance-level uncertainty monitoring. In this scenario, comparing uncertainty quantification (UQ) methods becomes challenging because LLM rankers lack a standard item-classification head. Their scores may depend on option labels, prompts, generation procedures, and the available user and item evidence. Existing methods derive uncertainty from different sources an...

item.title: LazUnirec: Unifying Retrieval and Ranking in Multi-scenario Industrial Recommendation
item.description: Modern industrial recommendation systems typically divide retrieval and ranking into two separate cascaded stages, leading to inconsistent optimization objectives, redundant encoding of user sequences, and a waste of computational resources. Previous efforts have investigated using Transformers to model both retrieval and ranking simultaneously. However, these studies still face two major limitations: (1) Since retrieval and ranking share a single Transformer backbone, the gradient conflict aris...

item.title: See the Answer, Learn to Embed: Learning Universal Multimodal Embeddings from Hindsight
item.description: Universal Multimodal Embedding (UME) models map heterogeneous multimodal inputs into a shared embedding space, where pairwise similarity supports diverse downstream tasks. Recent reasoning-driven UME approaches use intermediate reasoning to generate additional context for embedding, but often incur extra computation at inference. In this paper, we explore the matched candidate (i.e., the paired target) as an alternative source of context, asking whether a model can "see the answer" during traini...

item.title: Query Obfuscation with Embedding-Optimized Noise (EON): A Representational Blindspot in Agentic Retrieval
item.description: In modern agentic and semantic retrieval systems, dense embedding models increasingly determine which intent, tool, document, memory, or image to retrieve for a query. We identify a representational failure mode in this pipeline: a meaningful query can be replaced by visibly nonsemantic content while preserving much of its retrieval outcome, even when the candidate bank is hidden from the optimizer. We introduce Embedding-Optimized Noise (EON), constructed using only the natural query representa...

item.title: LARF: Learning-aligned Reasoning Framework for Search Relevance
item.description: Query-document relevance estimation is a core component of AI-native search systems, where a model must assess whether retrieved documents satisfy users' information needs under complex, multi-dimensional criteria. However, directly applying large language models (LLMs) to this task remains challenging because conventional supervised fine-tuning (SFT) provides limited supervision for domain-specific judgment rationales, while standard trajectory-level reinforcement learning (RL) objectives do no...

item.title: User-Adaptive Fusion of Multiple Foundation Models for Recommender Systems
item.description: Can recommender systems benefit from combining a collection of foundation models within and across modalities? While different foundation models may capture complementary aspects of item metadata, we find that naively combining their representations yields only marginal gains over using a single foundation model. We make a key observation: the users who benefit vary across foundation models. Motivated by this observation, we introduce UF2O, a user-adaptive approach for fusing multiple foundation...

item.title: MELODI: Similarity-Identity Decoupling for Lightweight Ranking
item.description: For latency-constrained candidate ranking, we propose a similarity-identity decoupling framework that separates target-history compatibility from target-only information. We study two orders for computing pooled similarity, similarity-then-pool and pool-then-similarity, and identify linearity of the similarity operator in its history argument, for each fixed target, as sufficient for their equivalence, justifying the cheaper pool-then-similarity form. We instantiate the framework as multi-head e...

item.title: OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval
item.description: Multimodal retrieval must match dense pages, fine-grained entities, ordered video, and agent tools and memory. Single-vector embeddings lose local evidence, cross-encoders reread every recalled item online, and uncompressed late interaction is too large to serve. We present OmniEVIE, a 4.5B multi-vector embedding model covering text, images, visual documents, video, and tools with one compressed index and a three-stage retriever. Each record stores at most 128 int8 vectors of dimension 64 (9,472...

item.title: ModernELECTRA: Replaced-Token Detection with Boundary-Window Reconstruction for Compact Encoders that Classify and Embed
item.description: ELECTRA-style replaced-token detection (RTD) is a sample-efficient objective for pre-training text encoders, and RTD-trained models such as DeBERTaV3 are strong on classification benchmarks. The same models, however, are known to be poor backbones for embedding tasks such as retrieval and semantic similarity: the binary "original vs. replaced" signal does not ask the final layer to retain the token identity and contextual content that dense representations rely on. We introduce ModernELECTRA, a ...

item.title: Speculative Decoding for Semantic-ID-Based Generative Recommendations
item.description: Generative recommender systems with Semantic IDs (SIDs) represent each item as a short sequence of $L$ discrete tokens and use a sequence model to predict the next item's tokens from a user's history. Industry-scale deployments typically use these models to retrieve multiple candidates per request with constrained beam search. However, this incurs a fixed cost of $L$ sequential model calls per request, and accuracy degrades as the SID generator becomes less sharp, without a guarantee on how clos...

item.title: A Text-to-SQL Benchmark for Official Statistics
item.description: Official statistics are critical datasets for a wide variety of actors, including policymakers and businesses. For providers of official statistics, improving accessibility, governance, and disclosure of their data is of key importance. This can be improved by providing question-answering systems based on text-to-SQL approaches. However, existing text-to-SQL benchmarks do not resemble this setting. Official statistics are published as open-domain catalogs of thousands of wide tables whose column...

item.title: Unjamming Deferrals: Supporting Students Through JAMN Bot, a Mobile RAG-Grounded Policy Assistant
item.description: In some educational institutions, workflows such as the exam deferral process can be slow, inconvenient, and inconsistent, which creates the need to implement novel digital systems. This paper presents Schedulater, a mobile app for managing university exam deferrals. JAMN Bot is a Large Language Model (LLM)-powered chatbot integrated into Schedulater that provides context-aware support to help users understand the deferral process. The system features a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipel...

item.title: Provenance Loss and Repair in Multilingual Compaction
item.description: Conversational assistants compact older messages into short notes and evict the originals. When the note's language requires a distinction that English leaves open, such as Spanish adjective gender (agotado vs. agotada), messages that omit or explicitly state that attribute can yield the same note. After eviction, later turns cannot tell them apart: taking the inflected form literally asserts an attribute the user never gave, whereas discounting it as routine grammar discards one the user did gi...

item.title: RELAY: Learning Compatible Representations One Encoder at a Time
item.description: Old and new document embeddings coexist during incremental gallery re-encoding. RELAY trains a new query encoder with a learned projection against the original gallery, then freezes both to train the new document encoder. The same query vector scores both document versions throughout a single re-encoding pass. After backfill, optional query refinement drops the projection and reuses the stored document vectors. Across three text-to-image retrieval upgrades on COCO and Flickr30K, RELAY improves R...

item.title: Provably Near-Optimal PQ in the Extended Zador Model
item.description: This paper investigates Product Quantization (PQ) Optimization with Gaussian data. It offers three key contributions (i) a proof that SVD is the optimal preconditioning rotation for PQ; (ii) a new Extended Zador (EZ) estimator of the $k$-means quantization cost that is accurate in low bit rates and low dimensions; and (iii) a novel segmentation algorithm based on 1-d bin packing of global bit allocations. The result is a simple algorithm (EZPQ) with strong approximation guarantees. It matches OP...

item.title: A dataset of clinically similar image pairs from citation-linked case reports for medical image retrieval
item.description: Retrieving images of patients clinically similar to a given patient can support diagnosis, teaching and research. Training and evaluating retrieval systems requires knowing which images of different patients show the same finding, and existing datasets are small or narrow in scope. We construct PMC-PaIR, a dataset of 86,144 pairs of clinically similar images from 56,013 open-access PubMed Central case reports, which often document rare or challenging presentations. We develop an approach that fo...

item.title: Small Learned Projections for Semantic-Reversal-Aware Retrieval with Spectral Acceleration: A Four-Domain Empirical Study
item.description: Dense-embedding retrievers can fail adversarially: when a query is answered by a document A and reversed by a near-copy B that differs from A by a small meaning-changing edit (a "trap"), raw cosine over E5-Large-v2 places B in the top-10 for 82-100% of queries at a pool of 5,000. We study two things. First, a small learned projection W: R^1024 -&gt; R^d (d in {11, 32}), trained by a deterministic recipe on a declared set of cases, that suppresses the trap: for the declared cases, HN@10 = 0.0000 ...

item.title: From Head to Tail: LLM-Augmented Sequential Recommendation and Trade-off Optimization
item.description: Recommender systems exhibit popularity bias, often under-serving long-tail and cold-start items with sparse interaction data. We propose a group-specific data augmentation approach that leverages LLMs to generate synthetic interactions, formulated as a constrained optimization problem, maximizing group-specific NDCG@20 and coverage while bounding overall NDCG@20 degradation within an acceptable threshold. Items are partitioned by interaction frequency to find the optimal augmentation strategy fo...

item.title: Ask Again: Answer-List Instability in Generative Engines
item.description: Visibility in generative search engines is measured by which entities appear in responses, and in what order. Ask an engine the same question twice and the answer list can change: a different ordering, or different items altogether. Across 60,000 responses, we find that answers to the same prompt name a different first item 32% of the time, and even two answers with the same items disagree on which comes first. The first position is a measurement target of its own. A &quot;clear leader&quot; emerges after...

item.title: CO-GRAFT: Attributing Reinforcement Learning Gains in Search Agents via Role-Level Policy Grafting
item.description: Reinforcement learning (RL) improves large language model search agents by up to 32 exact-match (EM) points over their pre-RL initializations, yet overall accuracy gains do not identify which underlying functional capabilities improve or interact during training. We introduce CO-GRAFT, a reward-agnostic interventional attribution framework in which an RL-trained agent and its pre-RL initialization jointly generate a single trajectory under closed-loop execution with live retrieval. Each policy c...

item.title: Orthogonally Mixed Sign Coding with Progressive Residual Refinement for Transformer Weight Compression
item.description: LLM quantization reduces storage but often degrades predictive fidelity at low bit rates. We propose a training-free, CDF-free, Gaussian-CLT-motivated progressive residual-sign quantization framework that uses randomized orthogonal mixing to promote Gaussian-like residual distributions and improve sign based reconstruction of Transformer weights. Each stage independently normalizes residuals and analytically calibrates reconstruction, progressively recovering quantization errors. The framework e...

item.title: Trallie: from Free-Form Text to Structured Data with LLMs
item.description: Trallie is an open-source framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) to perform information extraction (IE) from natural language sources with or without user guidance. Unlike conventional approaches that rely on extensive labeled datasets or domain-specific training, Trallie enables the conversion of unstructured data into structured formats with minimal or no representative examples. The framework is designed with three key objectives: (i) reducing manual annotation by harnessing pr...

item.title: Beyond Knowledge Transfer: How User Overlap Shapes Diversity in Cross-Domain Recommendation
item.description: A common paradigm in cross-domain recommendation (CDR) transfers knowledge through users shared by source and target domains. Although this overlap bridge is effective in improving accuracy, its effect on diversity remains unclear. We identify two bottlenecks: the bridge can be too narrow when overlapping users cover limited target-domain tastes, and too loud when shared signals dominate the sparse personal evidence of non-overlapping users. To address both, we propose DivCDR, a model-agnostic P...

item.title: SuSi-RAG: A Hybrid Graph RAG for Equipment Maintenance
item.description: In the manufacturing domain, equipment maintenance tasks depend on expert knowledge. Their documentation is often stored in heterogeneous formats and sources. The enhancement of LLMs with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is promising for bridging the scattered knowledge, but traditional vector-based RAG shows weaknesses with two characteristics which are common in real maintenance queries: complex causal chains and cross-domain synthesis. To address this, we propose SuSi-RAG, a hybrid Graph ...

item.title: Fetch, Read, Reuse: How AI Search Agents Bend the Web's Rules
item.description: AI search agents form a new and fast-growing class of web traffic. Like a browser, they fetch pages on demand for one user; like a transcoding proxy, they rewrite what they fetch; and like a shared cache, they answer other users&apos; questions from the stored copy. The rules publishers rely on, such as http://robots.txt, Retry-After, and Cache-Control, were written for more familiar clients, so the agent&apos;s vendor decides which of them to follow. We present a black-box measurement study of how these ...

item.title: PROSPER: LLMs as Sparse Retrievers for First-Stage Product Search
item.description: Product search is a crucial component of large-scale e-commerce platforms, where first-stage retrieval should achieve high recall while ensuring efficient online deployment. Sparse retrieval remains attractive for this setting due to its interpretability and deployability, yet it suffers from severe vocabulary mismatch challenges, especially for short queries and product titles. Large language models (LLMs) offer strong semantic capabilities, but directly applying them to sparse retrieval in pro...

item.title: Can Search Agents Correct Their Own Errors? Evaluating Retrieval, Evidence Delivery, and Answer Completion
item.description: A search agent can leave an earlier error unresolved by missing the right source, overlooking a relevant passage, or failing to revise and deliver the answer after receiving the evidence. We evaluate these possibilities on BrowseComp-Plus by replaying each model&apos;s own wrong closed-book answer in conversation and intervening on what evidence reaches the model. In a supplied-evidence study spanning four open-weight checkpoints, 709 questions and 26,665 test conditions, a confident assistant prior ...

item.title: Ontology-Compiled 2D Clinical State Fields with Bidirectional Diffusion Encoders for Zero-Training Cross-Ontology Medical Coding
item.description: Healthcare systems continually revise clinical taxonomies, update reimbursement schedules, and harmonize cross-border registries. Existing automated coding models bind clinical text understanding to fixed vocabulary-specific heads, requiring manual relabeling and retraining whenever code sets change. We introduce Ontology-Compiled 2D Clinical State Fields (OCSF), a vocabulary-free framework that decouples clinical document reading from target ontology indexing so one trained encoder can switch a...

item.title: Weight Coding: Evolving Web-Scale Recommenders through Direct Weight Edits with LLM Agents
item.description: Web-scale recommender models evolve primarily through retraining or fine-tuning. We propose \emph{weight coding}, a methodology for model evolution through direct, executable weight edits. A large language model (LLM) agent inspects model structure and parameters, formulates hypotheses, and implements edits using evaluation feedback. The loop progresses from localized changes to targeted searches and composition, allowing edited components to adapt to one another. A cached engine enables rapid f...

item.title: Pixel as the Common Language: Unified Multimodal Embedding via Visual Rendering
item.description: Multimodal embedding models map heterogeneous inputs into a shared representation space, yet text-only, image-only, and composed inputs are still presented in distinct formats and follow different routes through the model. This fragmentation prevents heterogeneous tasks from jointly optimizing the same end-to-end encoding process, limiting supervision transfer across input configurations. To address this issue, we propose unification before encoding and instantiate this paradigm in RenderEmbed. ...

item.title: STUN-Bench: Truly Unseen Tools for Evaluating Shared Tool Experience
item.description: A tool router retrieves a few candidate tools per request and lets a language model choose. Methods that share experience across organizations add past requests about each tool to what the router retrieves. StableToolBench calls some of its test groups tests on &quot;unseen&quot; tools, yet the ToolBench instruction pool, which retrievers and experience-sharing methods learn from, contains every test query and labels every gold tool of the two single-tool groups among them. We release STUN-Bench (StableTo...

item.title: SHAKTI: Evidence-Grounded Conversational AI for Nutrition and Health
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) answer many diet and health questions but can state unsupported claims and cite sources that do not support them. We present SHAKTI (Smart Health Advisor for Knowledge-based Tailored Interventions), a conversational assistant that answers only from retrieved scholarly papers and exact food-composition data, and evaluate it with retrieval, generation, grounding, efficiency and contextawareness metrics. We indexed 484,368,086 OpenAlex works, searched exactly on a GPU f...

item.title: Structure-Exploiting Hierarchical Retrieval for Long Narrative Documents: A Precision-Oriented Alternative to Learned Abstraction Trees
item.description: Retrieval-augmented generation over book-length documents must locate a small, coherent set of passages inside tens of thousands of tokens. Flat dense retrieval ignores document structure; RAPTOR instead builds a hierarchy by recursively clustering and summarizing with a language model. We study a complementary design that exploits the native structure of a document: a two-level retriever that (i) selects chapters with a hybrid BM25+dense match over chapter recaps, (ii) runs a chapter-filtered d...

item.title: Look Before You Leap: Re-Architecting Disk-Resident Vector Search with TriVS
item.description: Disk-resident approximate nearest-neighbor search (ANNS) scales vector search beyond DRAM, yet state-of-the-art systems remain I/O-bound, even with fast SSDs and sophisticated I/O execution. To understand this bottleneck, we conduct an I/O-centric analysis that breaks each query down into an approach phase that locates a query-near region and a converge phase that resolves the final top-k. This analysis reveals complementary I/O tradeoffs: cluster-based search circumvents approach-phase I/O thro...

item.title: Bridging Blind Spots With Words: Decentralized Multi-View Spatial Reasoning via Language-Constrained Communication
item.description: As multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) get increasingly used as collaborative partners across embodied robotics, AR/VR, and multi-user systems, spatial reasoning is now often distributed across agents with partial environment visibility, necessitating spatial reasoning integration. Prior work in language-mediated spatial integration is however strictly limited to simplified two-agent scenarios. To address this gap, we first formalize the general problem of decentralized multi-view spatial reasoning, where N...

item.title: Where Do Fact-Checking Errors Arise? Separating Retrieval, Search Control and Judgement in Evidence-Grounded Verification
item.description: An evidence-grounded fact-checker can fail because it does not find the evidence or because it does not use it; end-to-end accuracy does not tell the two apart. We present a protocol that follows the reference evidence from the store to the verdict and separates retrieval, search control, judgement and verdict validation. We assess 293 claims from FEVER, FEVER 2.0 and AVeriTeC with one open-weights 9B model under two evidence conditions: small stores of annotated evidence, where discovery is eas...

item.title: MoR4Rec: Mixture-of-Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
item.description: Sequential recommender systems aim to predict a user&apos;s next interaction by modeling temporal dependencies in historical behavior sequences. To capture such dependencies, recent approaches increasingly rely on attention-based architectures, particularly transformers. While effective at modeling long-range sequential patterns, these models apply a fixed computation depth to all interaction items, treating them as equally complex. However, user behavior is inherently heterogeneous, with many intera...

item.title: VistaTree: Question Answering over Long Multimodal Documents with Image-Derived Summary Trees
item.description: Answering questions over long multimodal documents requires locating relevant evidence across pages containing text, tables, and figures. When the document exceeds the model&apos;s context window, selective retrieval becomes necessary. We introduce VistaTree, a document question-answering agent that builds a summary tree directly from rendered page images. VistaTree segments documents into contiguous page spans, recursively groups them into a topic hierarchy, and refines sibling summaries to distingu...

item.title: LLM-Based Assistant for Dog Care Guidance
item.description: This study investigates whether domain grounding through Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and parameter-efficient fine-tuning using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) can enhance the accuracy and reliability of pet care advice generated by large language models (LLMs). We curated a dataset of breed-specific dog care information and used it to develop two systems: a RAG pipeline based on TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0, and a fine-tuned LLaMA-3.2-1B model adapted using LoRA. Both systems were evaluated on 1...

item.title: NoeVera: Can Knowledge Guide Experiments and Experiments Refine Knowledge?
item.description: With the growing demand for large language model (LLM) services, optimizing LLM serving systems is becoming increasingly complex, and the bottleneck is no longer predicting how a given configuration will perform. The harder problem is deciding what to investigate: which mechanisms matter for a workload, which configurations are worth testing, and what evidence a decision still needs. In this work, we present NoeVera, an agentic Second Brain that goes beyond just one-shot retrieval by turning pap...

item.title: Zarc: Exact Nearest Neighbors over a Billion Vectors in Seconds
item.description: Exact k-nearest-neighbor vector search lies on the critical path of machine learning systems, from sparse attention in the latest large language models (LLMs) to long-context memories and training-data deduplication. Exhaustive GPU search scans the whole dataset for every query, while approximate indexes return inexact neighbors. Recent methods skip almost every vector with a cheap half-precision proof that it lies too far away, but only on one GPU that holds the whole dataset. Our insight is to...

item.title: DataRecycle: Trustworthy Distillation of Structured Data from Scattered Web Evidence
item.description: The web contains vast amounts of scattered quantitative evidence that is difficult to organize into comparable and verifiable structures. Yet its unstructured, sparse, and sometimes conflicting nature makes a systematic distillation costly and error-prone. Existing approaches force users to make a trade-off: search engines return document lists that require labor-intensive extraction and reconciliation, while generative AI systems produce fluent summaries that obscure data provenance, introduce ...

item.title: HME-PFD: Heterogeneous Mixture-of-Experts Privileged Feature Distillation
item.description: Knowledge distillation (KD) is widely used to transfer knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, facilitating efficient serving of machine learning systems. In the context of ads recommendation, privileged features distillation (PFD) extends KD by allowing the teacher model to leverage privileged features, i.e., features available only during training, to enhance distillation performance. However, in real-world scenarios, privileged features often have limited coverage and e...

item.title: Who Gets Re-ranked When a Clinical Model Gains New Data?
item.description: Hospitals often update a deployed risk model by adding a data source, such as laboratory results, that only some patients have. Work on safe model updates assumes fixed inputs and so ignores patients who lack the new data. The update has no new measurements for them, yet their rank can change, and a sick patient not yet tested can drop off an alert list. item.title: ChatGPT Can't Sell (And That's Probably a Good Thing): Buyer-Aligned AI Advice, the Sales-Representative Gap, and Evidence from Commercial Conversations
item.description: AI assistants and merchant sales agents have different objectives: assistants should help buyers compare options and preserve the choice not to purchase, while sales agents also guide qualified buyers toward an authorized next step. item.title: MADRec: Reliable Multi-Agent Reasoning with Evidence-Grounded Debate for Recommendation
item.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) are transforming recommender systems from conventional preference matching toward reasoning-driven and explainable decision-making. Multi-agent collaboration further advances this paradigm by distributing recommendation reasoning across specialized agents. item.title: The abc index: Exact Retrieval for Learned Sparse Representations
item.description: In learned sparse retrieval (LSR), queries have tens of terms with learned weights, on which classic dynamic pruning is believed to fail, and approximate indexes such as Seismic and HNSW are considered faster than exact ones. item.title: Beyond Relevance: An Empirical Study of Multimodal LLMs for Diversity-Aware Recommendation Reranking
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) have emerged as promising rerankers for recommendation, yet most existing approaches rely on textual item descriptions and primarily focus on relevance. item.title: GERF: A Token-Efficient Multimodal Retrieval Framework for Schema-Guided Scientific Information Extraction
item.description: Scientific information extraction (IE) is a fundamental component of AI for Science, transforming experimental knowledge embedded in scientific literature into structured and traceable data for evidence synthesis, scientific database construction, and data-driven discovery. item.title: DM-Lab at TREC 2026 RAG: Multi-Query Retrieval, Ensemble Judging, and Claim-Pack Generation
item.description: We present DM-Lab-RAG-2026, a framework developed for the TREC 2026 Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) track. The framework integrates large-scale evidence retrieval and citation-grounded answer generation over the 553-million-document ClimbMix-400B corpus. item.title: Evaluating Memanto on DolphinBench for AI Agents
item.description: Memory benchmarks built on question answering tell an agent which fact to recall. Workplace requests often leave that need implicit: to post an update in the team&apos;s channel, an agent must work out which channel from earlier interactions and use it in a tool call. item.title: Which Dwarf Is This? Doppeldwarf-306 and Near-Identical Instance Retrieval
item.description: Most established instance-retrieval benchmarks emphasise landmarks; small sculptures from visually similar series offer a complementary challenge. item.description: Learning effective feature interactions is essential for industrial recommender systems. DCN and DCNv2 efficiently automate polynomial feature crossing. item.title: DiTraR: Diverse Scorers and Transcript-Guided Re-ranking for Video Corpus Moment Retrieval
item.description: Video corpus moment retrieval asks a system to find, in a large collection of untrimmed videos with subtitles, the video and the time interval that a natural-language query describes. item.title: Decision Columns as an Index: Interpretable Embeddings for Explainable Entity Matching and Search
item.description: Business data systems must determine whether records refer to the same entity and retrieve records satisfying requests whose decisive properties are implicit. item.description: Personalized long-form generation asks a language model to write new text the way a specific user would. item.title: Pre-Crawl Prioritization and Seed Classification for Large-Scale Web Archiving
item.description: Pre-crawl prioritization systems decide which pages to fetch first before indexing, aiming to improve crawl efficiency and coverage. item.description: Production retrieval systems are tied to the embedding model that indexed their corpus. item.title: Leader Finding: A New Variation of Expert Finding in Community Question Answering
item.description: Expert finding ranks people by their knowledge of a given topic. Many job positions need more than topical expertise, and a team leader is a clear case. A suitable leader knows the technical areas of the project without being overqualified, has strong managerial knowledge, and communicates well with the team. item.title: DNA: Unlocking Depth Scaling in CTR Models
item.description: Long user behavior sequences are among the strongest signals for click-through rate (CTR) prediction. item.description: Generative retrieval (GR) for sequential recommendation compresses each item into a short semantic ID and trains an autoregressive decoder to generate next-item codes from a user history. item.title: LINEAGE: A Benchmark for Empirical Lineage Retrieval in AI Scientific Literature
item.description: Current research agents are moving beyond academic search toward literature synthesis and experiment planning. These workflows increasingly rely on literature retrieval systems, which serve as standalone systems or as components of research agents. item.description: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a well-established paradigm for augmenting large language models (LLMs) with information retrieved from external corpora. item.title: LSP-RAG: Latent Scoring Perspectives for Knowledge Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation
item.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in open-domain question answering, but often struggle with factual accuracy and multi-hop reasoning due to the incompleteness of the training corpora. item.title: Cost-Aware Agentic Feature Optimization System for Fleet-Scale Ranking Models
item.description: Large Web platforms operate large fleets of ranking models, each selecting features from a shared pool of tens of thousands. item.title: From Sessions to Serving: Integrating LLM-Based Embeddings into Retrieval for Production Content Recommendation
item.description: Personalized content recommendation on large marketplace websites must reconcile heterogeneous candidate content (e.g., customer stories, product pages, industry pages, and learning content) with sparse, fast-changing user behavior, placing increasing demands on the retrieval stage to represent user interest well, not just the downstream ranking stage. item.description: Continuous generative retrievers powered by flow matching and diffusion sample multiple queries in item embedding space for parallel approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) search under fixed retrieval budgets. item.description: EU-funded projects produce extensive evidence in the form of deliverables, reports, and case studies. item.description: People often watch videos to find information, but locating relevant moments can be difficult and time-consuming. item.description: In recent decades, galleries, libraries, archives, and museums (GLAM institutions) have digitised vast amounts of cultural heritage material, including historical imagery. item.description: Resolving entity conflicts is a critical step in Pipeline-based NLU architectures, especially when multiple extractors provide overlapping or conflicting outputs. item.description: Text-based generative recommenders can go beyond ranking existing items by directly generating item titles or other textual representations. item.description: A recommendation page is consumed as a whole: the items on it compete for attention and complement one another, so the best page is not simply the individually best items placed side by side. item.description: The correspondence of Heinrich Bullinger (1504-1575), Swiss Reformer and Antistes of Zurich, documents the political and religious debates of the Reformation, including extensive appeals to the Church Fathers as authoritative sources. item.description: Large language model (LLM) judges have become a common way to create large-scale relevance judgments for retrieval evaluation.
